text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-pool-prod memory pressure > 92% across 3 nodes (node-17, node-21, node-22). Elevated CUDA OOM rate observed. Triggering incident workflow.

sam: taking it. pinging infra and runtime. reading logs now.

maria: saw a couple of container restarts ~10:12 on node-21, logs show "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" followed by runtime crash.

kyle: linking the dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-pool-prod/mem?from=now-2h to now - memory creeping up slowly on all paged-attn workers.

sam: initial triage: not an immediate spike — this is slow creep. hypothesis: paged-attention allocator or KV cache fragmentation causing ineffective free space -> OOM when high-concurrency requests hit.

ops-bot: Recent deploys: runtime v2.14.3 applied 1757998000 -> includes paged-attn allocator tweaks (fragmentation heuristics).

maria: logs snippet from node-21:
```
2026-05-14T10:11:47Z runtime[pid=8421]: WARNING: allocator: fragmented free blocks exceed threshold (frag_ratio=0.78)
2026-05-14T10:11:48Z runtime[pid=8421]: ERROR: failed to allocate 2097152 bytes: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
2026-05-14T10:11:48Z runtime[pid=8421]: INFO: kv-cache size: 1.8GB, eviction_policy=none
2026-05-14T10:11:48Z runtime[pid=8421]: fatal: uncaught exception -> container restart
```

sam: important: kv-cache reported at 1.8GB on these instances (we normally cap at 1.5GB). Did the deploy remove the cap?

kyle: yes, v2.14.3 introduced dynamic kv sizing to reduce misses, but might not enforce hard cap during fragmentation.

maria: quick mitigation options: 1) enable runtime env RW_PAGED_ATTN_ENABLE=false to bypass paged-attn allocator 2) set KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=1200000000 and force eviction 3) rolling-restart affected nodes after setting envs 4) temporarily route traffic away from node-21.

sam: mitigation plan — two phases: immediate (reduce customer impact) and corrective. Immediate: set KV cap and enable eviction, flip off paged-attn on the runtime workers on node-21/node-22; do rolling restart with drain so we don't spike latencies. Corrective: revert allocator change in v2.14.3 and run a memory-fw regression/bench for fragmentation, add fragmentation metrics & OOM alerting.

maria: executing immediate changes on node-21 now. running:
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/runtime-worker RW_PAGED_ATTN_ENABLE=false --overwrite
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/runtime-worker KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=1200000000 --overwrite
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/runtime-worker --selector=pool=prod,zone=node-21
```

incident-bot: action logged by maria at 10:24 UTC: env toggle + rollout-start. Estimated drain time 45s per pod.

kyle: routing: I'll update the LB to reduce new sessions to node-21 until pods back up. Doing incremental connection reduction: set max-sessions on node-21 -> 0.7x.

sam: monitoring: watching OOM count and free GPU memory metrics.

(5 minutes pass)

maria: node-21 pods are back up, KV cap applied, eviction visible: kv-cache dropped from 1.8GB -> 1.1GB on restarted pods. Memory usage decreased ~14% across node-21. No immediate OOM on node-21.

kyle: node-22 still showing slow leak, starting same changes there.

sam: customer impact check — looking at request error rates.

sam: customers impacted (observed errors 10:05-10:25 UTC):
- customer-alpha (prod): spikes in 502s across session creation, ~4% of requests failed, bursty timeouts.
- partner-b (dedicated): experienced 1 pod restart, degraded tail latency from 120ms -> 520ms for ~6 minutes.
- internal-qa: test jobs failed intermittently (non-prod).

maria: posting incident severity recommendation: SEV-2 (service degraded, partial customer impact, mitigation in-flight).

ops-bot: note: recent allocation change id: deploy/1757998000 -> patch 2.14.3/alloc-frag-heuristic. Linking PR: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4281

kyle: after flipping env on node-22 and rolling restart, both node-21 and node-22 stabilized. node-17 still trending up, scheduling restart there too but will do staggered to avoid capacity drop.

sam: timeline so far: 10:12 alert -> 10:24 first mitigation on node-21 -> 10:31 node-21 stable -> 10:38 node-22 changes -> 10:50 node-22 stable -> 10:55 node-17 scheduled change.

maria: temporary mitigations applied:
- RW_PAGED_ATTN_ENABLE=false (per-pod env)
- KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=1200000000 and eviction=LRU triggered
- rolling restart with drain on affected zones
- LB reduced sessions to nodes during restarts

sam: handoff to night on-call (kyle) in 30m. leaving the remaining corrective actions and postmortem notes.

kyle: I'll take over. immediate runbook for night on-call:
1) monitor OOM metric (runtime.cuda_oom.count) and mem_free_gpu per node -> pager if >2 OOMs in 10m
2) if creeping memory observed, flip RW_PAGED_ATTN_ENABLE=false across the pool and schedule a coordinated rolling restart with 10% concurrency cap
3) prepare revert PR for v2.14.3 allocator tweak and run perf/fuzz on a staging pool with high-concurrency KV workload
4) add fragmentation ratio and KV fragmentation metric to dashboards + an alert at frag_ratio > 0.6 for 10m

sam: notes for postmortem: probable root cause = paged-attention allocator fragmentation exacerbated by removal of hard KV cache cap in v2.14.3, causing large fragmentation + missed evictions -> slow memory creep -> CUDA OOM under burst. Recommend revert + more conservative dynamic sizing + hard cap + eviction + fragmentation monitoring.

maria: I'll create a follow-up issue with logs + heap snapshots + CUDA device free snapshots; will attach cron job to collect memory maps every 5m during repro.

kyle: customer communication: propose briefing to customer-alpha and partner-b: summarize impact, actions taken, ETA for permanent fix (48-72 hours), offer support contacts. ops-comms, please draft.

incident-bot: ACTION: incident transitioned to "mitigated" at 11:03 UTC by kyle. On-call handoff declared.

kyle: handing over to night on-call. current state: pool stable, OOM events back to baseline, KV cache enforced at 1.2GB on all prod pods, paged-attn disabled until allocator patch lands. Follow-ups: revert PR + extended testing, add fragmentation alerting, postmortem.

sam: thanks team. please add any logs or follow-ups to the incident ticket: INC-2026-2157.

maria: filing INC-2026-2157/notes and linking PRs now. :white_check_mark:

kyle: leaving final status update for handoff: stable, partial customer impact, mitigations in place. will monitor overnight. :hand: :eyes:
